messages:
claira: Heads-up — nodepool 'gpu-eu-west-accelerated' has 3 nodes stuck in Terminating. ClusterAutoscaler isn't replacing them and inference pods are Pending. We're at 0 available GPU capacity for prod-eu.

ben: Ouch. Any events on those nodes? kubelet logs?

claira: Quick dump:
```
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide | egrep 'gpu-eu-west|NotReady|Terminating'
ip-10-1-23-45.eu-west   Ready,SchedulingDisabled   1/1   gpu  10.1.23.45
ip-10-1-24-11.eu-west   Terminating                0/1   gpu  10.1.24.11
ip-10-1-25-90.eu-west   Terminating                0/1   gpu  10.1.25.90
```
Events on one terminating node show cloud-provider detach delays and "instance is shutting down" loops. CA logs: "Node group not safe to scale: 3 instances terminating".

priya: If CA sees terminating instances it will refuse to scale the group. We need capacity quick. Can we move the highest-priority pods to a temp pool?

ken: Two quick options: 1) force-create a small temporary nodepool without the problematic instance template and patch critical deployments to schedule there, or 2) create a new nodegroup + cordon the terminating nodes and patch the CA to ignore deleting instances for a minute. I prefer #1 — less fiddly.

devops-oncall: Spawning temp pool now (eksctl):
```bash
eksctl create nodegroup --cluster=redwood-prod-eu --name=temp-gpu-quick --node-type=p4d.xlarge --nodes=2 --nodes-min=1 --nodes-max=3 --labels=pool=temp-gpu,ephemeral=true
```
Estimated bootstrap ~90s. Pushing a temp nodeSelector to the top-priority workload:
```bash
kubectl patch deployment inference-highprio -n prod --type='json' -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/nodeSelector","value":{"pool":"temp-gpu"}}]'
```

ben: Nice. Are we preserving QoS/priority so autoscaler doesn't evict them?

priya: We set PodPriority for highprio jobs already. After the patch pods should land on temp pool. I'll watch for image pull errors.

sre-bot: [autoscaler] Notice: scale-up event requested for nodegroup temp-gpu-quick -> +2 nodes.

claira: Pods started popping onto temp pool, inference traffic back to normal (some increased tail latency while caches warm). CA still shows stuck terminating nodes — need follow-up with cloud infra.

ken: For immediate mitigation we also patched CA flags to be more lenient (rolled back after). Logged exact command in the incident ticket.

devops-oncall: Confirming teardown plan: once stuck nodes finish terminating we'll drain and delete temp pool. Leaving temp pool autoscaling min=1 for 1 hour to handle burst.

priya: Postmortem action items: 1) Add alert when CA reports 'terminating instances blocking scale', 2) Investigate cloud API termination latency and instance lifecycle hooks, 3) Add runbook step to create ephemeral nodepool + nodeSelector patch.

claira: Mitigated: high-priority inference served from temp nodes, overall capacity restored. Filing follow-up ticket: INFRA-1287. Thanks all :heart:
